item.title: Building Effective Community-Academic Partnerships: Lessons from Project GRACE — Wed Aug 5, 10:00 AM
item.description:
Join us for an interactive session exploring how meaningful partnerships between academic institutions and community organizations can strengthen community health initiatives. Drawing on lessons from Project GRACE, a community-academic partnership with more than 20 years of experience in eastern North Carolina, presenters will share practical strategies for community engagement, relationship building, shared decision-making, and sustainable collaboration. Participants will gain a better understanding of community-engaged and participatory research approaches and leave with actionable ideas for applying these principles in their own work.
Register for Building Partnerships!
Presenters are Mysha Wynn, Erika Redding and Mary McKinley.
This session is part of the Connections that Count: Abacus Evaluation Community Engagement Webinar Series.
Source: UNC Chapel Hill

Health Assessments are available to all active Duke employees.

item.title: Circles of Influence: Social Network Analysis for Community-Engaged Evaluation Research — Wed Aug 12, 10:00 AM
item.description:
This webinar introduces the fundamentals of social network analysis within the context of community-engaged evaluation research. It will begin with the underlying theory behind networks and how we build them with an emphasis on relationships, trust, and community connections. We'll share several case studies to illustrate how we use networks in impact reporting and evaluation research. Participants will gain insight into how network approaches can center community voices, connect partnerships, and enhance evaluation practices.
Register for Circles of Influence!
Bernard Coles is presenting.
This session is part of the Connections that Count: Abacus Evaluation Community Engagement Webinar Series.
Source: UNC Chapel Hill

item.title: Pop The Cap | Anniversary Discussion and Toast — Thu Aug 13, 5:00 PM — Fullsteam ATC
item.description:
It's been 21 years since former North Carolina Governor Mike Easley signed HB 392 into law, raising the state's Alcohol by Volume (ABV) limit for beer from 6% to 15%. Fullsteam founder and owner Sean Lilly Wilson organized that movement, allowing brewers across the state to offer a much wider variety of products to beer drinkers. Come join him and others at Fullsteam's new ATC location for a panel discussion about the legacy of this legislation and all things beer in the Old North State, followed by beer and cake!
Source: American Tobacco Campus

Durham Writers Group We will be at the Moon House at 3039 University Dr. in Durham. This venue does not serve food or drink, but feel free to bring your own. There is a kitchenette for our use, but be sure to clean up afterwards. The space might be a little cozy; please consider masking or staying home if you have a respiratory ailment.
This sub-group focuses on Speculative Fiction, including Science Fiction, Fantasy and Horror. If you have anything that falls under that category — be it short story, poem, novel-in-progress or screenplay — then come! We'd love to hear from you.
Our format allows each reader 15 minutes to present their work aloud, followed by approximately 20 minutes of feedback from the other attendees. To ensure fairness, each attendee is limited to 1 minute of Initial Feedback time. During that period, the author remains silent. Next, we have a 5 minute Free-For-All discussion about the work -- then the author may speak. (We usually get through three readers.)

item.title: Intermediate Qualtrics — Mon Oct 26, 3:00 PM
item.description:
This course will cover topics beyond the scope of the Introductory to Qualtrics short course. We will take a deeper dive into Survey Flow features including embedded data, customizing the End of Survey experience, Screen Out Management, and implementing randomization. We will explore methods of importing embedded data into your survey, sending information from one survey to another, and setting embedded data in your survey through conditions within your survey. An introduction to automations will be illustrated through an example use case that sends respondents to a drawing survey after completing their survey. Finally, we will create custom reports to share with others in the ‘reports’ tab. Course material will be incorporated into a shared Group in which all participants will be added, offering hands-on practice with shared Libraries, and Directories. Additional features to be discussed include piping, authentication, and version management.
Registration and fee are required for Zoo

We will warm the body, moving in a way that encourages each dancer to better honor and understand their unique physicality. Next, dancers will explore different ways to generate movement phrases. item.description: Join North Carolina’s Artemis Sportswomen ambassador Lisa Fierman for an introduction to deer hunting. We invite you to learn more about the relationship between hunting and conservation and the tenets of an ethical hunter. This presentation will include an overview of the skills and knowledge it takes to become a successful deer hunter, and how to find a place to hunt. Artemis Sportswomen is an official program of the National Wildlife Federation and invests in the long-term health and vitality of the sporting world by advancing women’s leadership. By investing in sportswomen’s communities, skills, and leadership, Artemis continues to create an intergenerational cohort of outdoors leaders and champions for hunting and angling. Artemis is dedicated to creating lasting positive impact on sporting and the outdoors, and the land, water, and wildlife upon which we all depend. item.title: Trail Talks with TLC: Brumley North — Fri Jul 31, 9:00 AM — Brumley North Nature Preserve
item.description:
Get a special look at TLC's work on this staff led hike series! Join TLC Grants Manager, Laura Warman, and Working Lands Manager, Emma Childs, on an exploration of Brumley North Nature Preserve. Learn about the forest ecology within the various habitats of Brumley that have made this preserve a popular spot for birders, hikers, bikers, and naturalists! This is a free event, but preregistration is required.

item.title: What A Ranger Does - World Ranger Day — Fri Jul 31, 10:00 AM — Near Cliffdwellers
item.description:
Join us as we celebrate World Ranger Day! Our Park Rangers work hard to keep our parks and public lands open, safe, and accessible for all. Did you know that many rangers are also firefighters, EMTs, police officers, and more? Meet a Park Ranger and learn about the many hats a Park Ranger wears.
This touch-a-truck style program will give you a hands-on look at the gear, training, and daily work that goes into protecting the Park.
Around the globe, park rangers are on the front line in the fight to protect our natural heritage. World Ranger Day offers a chance to support their vital work, which ranges from environmental campaigning to education. The day is also an opportunity to pay tribute to rangers who have lost their lives in the line of duty.
***Free with Admission to Chimney Rock Attraction***
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.description:
Durham: the mecca of black capitalism and the center of North Carolina’s African American business community. Join a local historian on this guided walking tour of Durham’s Black Wall Street, hearing the stories of how a humble sharecropper became the owner of the largest black-ned company in American history, and seeing some of the sites related to their stories. Learn how businessmen, labor organizers, educated academics, and craftsmen each contributed to the unique history of Durham’s African American community.

item.description:
Explore the spooky side of Durham’s history on this tour of the city’s most haunted locations. From the disgraced sons of tobacco giants who continue to roam their old factories, to tales of tragic accidents whose victims still haunt the site of their end, and murder victims who stubbornly cling to their possessions, Durham, NC, has a shadowy side to its history. Travel through the city with the assistance of a professional historian guide, while hearing about the city’s creepiest folklore.

item.description:
Triple Tar Heel and science communicator Mejs Hasan will deliver the keynote address at the 2026 Royster Global Conference, which is also the celebration of the 30th anniversary of the Royster Society of Fellows.
Today’s challenges, like environmental degradation, migration, and social division, don’t fit neatly within the confines of a single discipline. In order to really address them, we have to cross diverse boundaries, pulling together wisdom from different times, geographies, and subject matters. For 30 years, the Royster Society of Fellows has embodied this spirit of crossing boundaries. It has encouraged and supported collaborations between the science and the humanities, despite their perceived differences.

item.description:

Leave when you need to!
